P. Road, Kilikolloor, Kollam, Pin - 691004 Represented By Managing Partner Naufal Salam, By Advs. Aswin Gopakumar Anwin Gopakumar Aditya Venugopalan Mahesh Chandran Saranya Babu Abhishek S. Tanya Kadeeja Anjana A. Respondents: 1 The Commissioner Of Customs Department Of Revenue, Ministry Of Finance, Custom House, Indira Gandhi Road, Willingdon Island, Cochin, Pin - 682009 2 The Additional Commissioner Of Customs Department Of Revenue, Ministry Of Finance, Custom House, Indira Gandhi Road, Willingdon Island, Cochin, Pin - 682009 By Adv Girish Kumar V This Writ Petition (Civil) Having Come Up For M/S Tasty Nut Industries vs The Commissioner Of Customs on 3 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139191765/ 1 Admission On 03.04.2025, The Court On The Same Day Delivered The Following: 2025:Ker:28623 W.P.(C). texts.facts: Petitioner seeks for a direction to permit the goods covered by Ext.P3 Bill of Entry to be cleared for re-export after re-processing, by permitting it to be moved to a customs bonded premises. 2. Petitioner is a manufacturer and exporter of cashew based products. In the year 2022, 400 cartons of about 8000 Kg of organic cashew kernels were exported by the petitioner. However, since the foreign buyer rejected the goods due to an alleged mis-match of the label, the goods were re - imported claiming the benefit of Customs Notification No. 45/2017 . However, the customs subjected the imported goods to certification by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI). The said Authority rejected 200 cartons of cashew kernels out of the total 400 cartons stating those to be unfit for home consumption. Subsequently, petitioner amended the Bill of Entry claiming the benefit of Notification No.158/1995 and indicated that they were ready to execute necessary bonds promising to re-export the goods after re-processing. However, the Commissioner of Customs ordered confiscation stating that the amendment of Bill of Entry was an afterthought. 2025:KER:28623 3. Challenging the said order of confiscation, petitioner approached the Customs, Export Service Tax Appellate Tribunal, Bengaluru ('CESTAT'), pointing out that since the products have been undertaken to be re-exported and also since the goods are not unfit for human consumption but only that, the standards of FSSAI were not met, nothing prevents them from re-exporting goods after re- processing. CESTAT allowed Customs Appeal No.20010/2024 by order dated 04-06-2024 and directed the petitioner to re-process the same by dry heating within the premises of the Customs and re-export the goods at the earliest. While so, since the petitioner found it difficult to carry out dry heating within the customs premises, an application was filed for modification of the order of the CESTAT, to permit the petitioner to carry out the process within the premises of its factory. However, observing that the Tribunal does not have the jurisdiction to review its own orders, the said application was dismissed. 4. In the meantime, petitioner's factory was designated as a 100% Export Oriented Unit (EOU) on 23.10.2024 with all the permissions from the Customs to treat its premises as a customs bonded premises. Since petitioner can carry out re-processing work within its own bonded premises, it M/S Tasty Nut Industries vs The Commissioner Of Customs on 3 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139191765/ 2 being designated as a 100% EOU, petitioner has approached this Court, seeking the directions mentioned earlier. 2025:KER:28623 5. Customs Department has objected to the prayers pointing out that petitioner ought to have approached the Customs Authorities for such permissions and further that, removal of the cargo for re- processing them for re-export require re-assessment of the subject Bill of Entry to provide the benefit of the MFDR notification No.52/2003 and hence the petitioner ought to have approached the jurisdictional Customs Authorities. 6.
